text.title: Schema Split / Post-Validate / Two-Call Decision Tree
text.summary: Routing from observable schema and request properties to an action. Read the first branch that matches; the last two branches are overlays that apply regardless of which earlier branch fired.

decision-tree.root-question: Does the schema contain any keyword beyond type, `enum`, `const`, `required` and `additionalProperties: false` — that is, any `minimum`, `maximum`, `multipleOf`, `minLength`, `maxLength`, `pattern`, `maxItems`, or `minItems` other than 0 or 1?

conclusion.verdict: STOP. Types, enums, required and additionalProperties are compiled, so the written schema and the enforced schema coincide. No split, no record. Keep it that way: the next range you add reopens this tree.
Split the file. Wire schema keeps the compiled subset; validation schema keeps the full contract. Write the record, and give every computed drop a checker and a counter before shipping.
Split, then take the UNION of the per-transport drop sets and post-validate at that strictest level on every path. Do not let one provider's grammar be the reason a value is well-formed.

branch.when: semantic_keywords_present == true AND post_validation_exists == true AND counters_exist == false

conclusion.verdict: The check exists and is unobservable. Promote every log line to a counter on the result object and assert on it in the eval harness. This is the cheapest reliability change available here.

Two calls, not one. Call 1: structured output, no citations, emits identifiers. Call 2: citations enabled over the bodies of exactly those identifiers, no `output_config.format`. A single request returns 400.
Overlay. Strip it deliberately and record where the constraint moved. Leaving it is a coin flip between silent stripping and a 400, and it inflates the compiled grammar toward the size limit.
Overlay. Add at least one semantic metric over the dropped keywords before spending anything on raising compliance; compliance is already the saturated number.
